title: Merge with explicit key, null, clause and duplicate semantics
brief: Merge composes a source DataFrame, target snapshot and ordered conditional actions. Decide null-key and duplicate-source policy before treating it as an upsert.

choices.choose_when: Different matched/unmatched cases need different actions
choices.tradeoff: Aliases and ordered predicates define the semantics

choices.choose_when: Source data is already a complete replacement slice or pure append
choices.tradeoff: Simpler input contract; no source-target action matrix

choices.choose_when: Multiple source rows can match one target with conflicting updates
choices.tradeoff: Requires an application-defined tie-break rule; do not silently drop duplicates

claims.statement: The first applicable matched update won in the probe; source and target null keys did not match under ordinary equality. Unmatched insert and by-source delete contributed independently.
Two matching source rows attempting to update one target produced an error and left the observed version unchanged in the tested case.
when_* takes a closure configuring a merge clause builder. Its UpdateBuilder/DeleteBuilder types are not constructors for standalone table update/delete operations.
Await returns updated table plus MergeMetrics; interpret inserted/updated/deleted counts in the context of source multiplicity and chosen clauses.

implementation: Use explicit source/target aliases and qualified columns.
Choose equality versus a deliberate null-safe condition and independently specify duplicate-source handling.
Assert rows, versions and per-action metrics; a completed merge is not evidence of an application-level unique key.
errors: Invalid expressions, ambiguous/multiple matches, protocol/schema restrictions and optimistic conflicts require distinct recovery.
unknowns: Every schema-evolution/duplicate-delete combination and concurrency schedule is not certified by the selected fixture.

evidence.scope: Exact git-capture full contracts for the selected operations
Pinned delta-rs implementation; full file retained with acquisition provenance
Named local assertions only; see profile, fixtures and source digests
